# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

## CFP Registration

FACT: Registered parties must "Register with DEQ before producing fuel in Oregon, importing fuel into Oregon, dispensing certain fuels into motor vehicles, or generating or transacting credits for fuels supplied in Oregon." *Source: Oregon DEQ Clean Fuels Program Overview, Oregon DEQ, active as of 2026. https://www.oregon.gov/deq/ghgp/cfp/pages/cfp-overview.aspx

*Operational implication:* Registration is a pre-activity obligation. It must occur before fuel is imported or dispensed in Oregon, not retroactively. For workspaces that have recently commenced Oregon fuel-related operations, this creates a registration gap risk if the DEQ-defined trigger point for "importing" has already been crossed.

## CFP Record-Keeping

FACT: Registered parties must "Keep records for each transaction of transportation fuel imported, sold or supplied for use in Oregon." *Source: Oregon DEQ Clean Fuels Program Overview, Oregon DEQ, active as of 2026. https://www.oregon.gov/deq/ghgp/cfp/pages/cfp-overview.aspx

*Operational implication:* Transaction-level tracking, not summary or aggregate tracking, is required. Workspaces using aggregate fuel purchase accounting (total monthly diesel spend rather than per-transaction volume records) would not satisfy this requirement.

## CFP Quarterly and Annual Reporting

FACT: Registered parties must "Submit quarterly and annual reports using the Oregon Fuels Reporting System." *Source: Oregon DEQ Clean Fuels Program Overview, Oregon DEQ, active as of 2026. https://www.oregon.gov/deq/ghgp/cfp/pages/cfp-overview.aspx

*Operational implication:* The Oregon Fuels Reporting System is the exclusive submission platform for CFP compliance data. Any workspace that is a registered party and that does not have system access configured will not be able to meet the quarterly reporting obligation.

## Pollution Complaint and Public Notice Infrastructure

FACT: Oregon DEQ provides a "File a Pollution Complaint" mechanism and maintains public notice infrastructure for regulatory proceedings. *Source: Oregon DEQ Welcome Page, Oregon DEQ, active as of 2026. https://oregon.gov/deq/Pages/index.aspx

*Analytical inference:* For freight operations with Oregon facilities, the pollution complaint mechanism creates a community-facing accountability channel. Operations in proximity to environmental justice communities face an elevated probability that pollution events (e.g., diesel spills, air emissions incidents) will generate DEQ complaint investigations.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

## CFP Reporting System Access

**Scope:** Any workspace that is a registered CFP party (mandatory or voluntary).

**Gap from current operational baseline:** *Operational implication:* Freight forwarding workspaces without existing state environmental reporting system accounts would need to establish Oregon Fuels Reporting System credentials, configure transaction-level fuel data feeds, and train personnel on quarterly submission workflows before the first quarterly deadline falls. See section 10 above for the underlying registration, record-keeping, and reporting duties this system serves.

## Vehicle Inspection Compliance Tracking

**Scope:** Oregon road fleet operations.

*Operational implication:* Workspaces operating vehicle fleets in Oregon should maintain records of DEQ vehicle inspection compliance for each fleet unit, including inspection dates, station location, and pass/fail outcomes. Failure to produce these on demand during an enforcement inspection would constitute a compliance gap. See section 3 above for the Clean Air Stations list.

## Statewide Transportation Strategy Alignment

*Operational implication:* For workspaces with medium- and heavy-duty truck operations in Oregon, the multi-agency Statewide Transportation Strategy implementation (section 5 above) may generate additional regulatory requirements through parallel rulemaking at ODOT, DLCD, and the Department of Energy, not only through DEQ. Monitoring these adjacent agencies' rulemaking pipelines is operationally necessary.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

## CFP Exemptions and Technology Neutrality

*Analytical inference:* The CFP "The CFP is intended to be technology neutral and applies to the average of on-road transportation fuels used in the state with exemptions for fuels used in small volumes or for agriculture and logging." *Source: Stillwater CFP 101, Stillwater Associates, May 29, 2026. https://stillwaterpublications.com/stillwater-cfp-101/

*Operational implication:* For workspaces with clients in agriculture or logging sectors, fuels supplied or arranged for those end uses may be exempt from CFP CI accounting. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the precise definitional boundary of the agriculture and logging exemption under OAR 340-253, including whether it applies at the fuel supplier level or the end-use level, and whether a freight forwarder arranging fuel logistics for an exempt end use inherits the exemption. This is the pool's only exemption language for the CFP; it uses the morphological form "exemptions," never the word-boundary form "exempt," which is why section 8's qualification accounting records the operative sections as stating no such clause directly.

## CFP Forward Scope (why "scope" is not counted as a current scope limit)

FACT: "Oregon’s CFP is a living regulation, neither stagnant nor operating in a void. We expect changes to both the scope and reduction schedule in the years to come." *Source: Stillwater CFP 101, Stillwater Associates, May 29, 2026. https://stillwaterpublications.com/stillwater-cfp-101/

*Analytical inference:* This is the pool's only occurrence of the word "scope." It describes Stillwater's own expectation of future rulemaking changes, not a present legal restriction on which entities or activities the CPP or CFP currently binds. Section 8's qualification accounting therefore records no current scope limit from this sentence.

## Supplemental Environmental Projects (Penalty Reduction)

FACT: "DEQ encourages violators to consider Supplemental Environmental Projects , which provide Oregon with direct environmental benefits. These projects cover a wide range of environmental improvements, including habitat restoration, household hazardous waste collection events, wood stove change out grants, or funding to help school districts retrofit older school buses to use clean-diesel technology." *Source: Oregon DEQ Compliance and Enforcement, Oregon DEQ, active as of 2026. https://www.oregon.gov/DEQ/Regulations/Pages/Compliance-and-Enforcement.aspx

*Operational implication:* In the event of a DEQ enforcement action, a workspace may negotiate a Supplemental Environmental Project to reduce the cash penalty amount. The SEP must provide direct environmental benefit and be approved by DEQ. The clean-diesel bus retrofit example cited is operationally adjacent to freight sector interests.

FACT: "For more information, see the full rule in the Oregon secretary of State Archives: Division 12 - Enforcement Procedure and Civil Penalties" *Source: Oregon DEQ Compliance and Enforcement, Oregon DEQ, active as of 2026. https://www.oregon.gov/DEQ/Regulations/Pages/Compliance-and-Enforcement.aspx

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

## Multi-State LCF Program Landscape

*Analytical inference:* Stillwater Associates' industry analysis indicates that the regulatory burden on diesel-consuming freight operators is expanding geographically across the U.S. West Coast and beyond, with Oregon, Washington, and New Mexico all having adopted LCF programs and additional states in legislative consideration. This creates a scenario where the workspace's cross-border road operations face stacked, non-identical carbon intensity compliance systems.

FACT: Washington and New Mexico adopted their own low carbon fuel programs, "as did Washington state in 2023 with an effective date of 2024 and New Mexico in 2024 with an effective date in 2026 – the interactions among programs may require program adjustments." *Source: Stillwater CFP 101, Stillwater Associates, May 29, 2026. https://stillwaterpublications.com/stillwater-cfp-101/

FACT: "most recently by New Mexico’s Clean Transportation Fuel Program (CTFP), which became effective April 1, 2026." *Source: Stillwater CFP 101, Stillwater Associates, May 29, 2026. https://stillwaterpublications.com/stillwater-cfp-101/

FACT: "Hawaii passed LCF program legislation in 2026 that is awaiting the Governor’s signature, and additional state programs are under active consideration in Illinois, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, and Vermont." *Source: Stillwater CFP 101, Stillwater Associates, May 29, 2026. https://stillwaterpublications.com/stillwater-cfp-101/

*Operational implication:* For a freight forwarding workspace with road operations across multiple U.S. states, the proliferation of state-level low-carbon fuel programs materially increases the probability that diesel consumption in multiple jurisdictions will become subject to credit-deficit accounting, each with distinct CI schedules, fuel pathway registries, and annual deadlines.

## DEQ Workplan and Fleet Electrification

FACT: "Below are links to work plan projects that DEQ will take a leading role to implement: Expand Clean Fuels Program Truck Alternatives Fuels Study and Implementation Statewide Trip Reduction (also known as the Employee Commute Option Program) Parking Management New Emissions Standards and ZEV Requirements for Medium- and Heavy-Duty Trucks" *Source: Oregon DEQ Implementation of the Statewide Transportation Strategy, Oregon DEQ, active as of 2026. https://www.oregon.gov/deq/ghgp/Pages/Transportation-Strategy.aspx

FACT: "Below are links to work plan projects that DEQ will take a supporting role to implement: Interagency Zero Emission Vehicle (ZEV) Action Plan" *Source: Oregon DEQ Implementation of the Statewide Transportation Strategy, Oregon DEQ, active as of 2026. https://www.oregon.gov/deq/ghgp/Pages/Transportation-Strategy.aspx

*Analytical inference:* Fleet electrification of Oregon road operations is both a CPP/CFP compliance strategy (reducing diesel-sourced deficits) and a subject of active multi-agency regulatory development. Workspaces that invest in electric road vehicles in Oregon may simultaneously reduce their CPP compliance instrument exposure and position favorably ahead of forthcoming ZEV mandates for medium- and heavy-duty trucks.
